description:
`required_resume_transport_positions` (src/compiler2/jobs/artifact.rs:733-782)
builds `deliver_callsites: HashMap<ControlEntryId, CallSiteId>` with a plain
`.insert()` at line 762. When more than one callsite delivers into the same
target entry, whichever the iteration reaches LAST silently wins, and only that
callsite appears in the `TransportPosition::ResumePayload` returned at line 775.

## Why this matters more than when it was filed

`callsite` is part of position IDENTITY, not a classification:
`TransportPosition::ResumePayload { executable, callsite: Option<CallSiteId>,
entry }` (transport.rs:344-348) derives `Hash`/`Eq` over all three fields. The
two mint sites therefore disagree:

- `required_resume_transport_positions` produces ONE position per
  delivered-resume entry, arbitrary callsite.
- `call_return_flow` (artifact.rs:1509-1557) produces
  `ResumePayload { callsite: Some(callsite), entry }` for EVERY delivering
  callsite.

The losing callsite's `CallReturnFlow::Deliver` therefore names a position absent
from `position_layouts`, so backend.rs:1577-1589 never mints its
`CodegenSeam::ContinuationEntry { executable, callsite, entry }`.

## The multi-deliver case comes from ordinary source

jobs/body.rs:2726-2760: a non-tail `If` creates ONE join `resume` entry and
passes `ControlDestination::Deliver(resume)` to BOTH branch blocks, so a call in
tail position of each branch delivers into the same entry from two distinct
callsites:

    fn g(x), do: x + 1
    fn f(c) do
      y = if c do g(1) else g(2) end
      y + 10
    end
    fn main() do
      dbg(f(true)); dbg(f(false))
    end

    $ fz2 interp repro.fz
    12
    13

Output is CORRECT today -- `call_return_flow`'s Deliver arm never calls
`require_transport_layout` on `resume`, so the mismatch does not reach a consumer
that requires the layout. This is a latent arbitrary-survivor, not a live
miscompile. It was established by reading the two mint sites, not by a captured
failure: `TransportPosition` values do not appear in the backend/native/fnir
dumps.

## What the old ticket got wrong

It named `collect_resume_entries` at jobs/transport.rs:2656-2701. That function
is GONE (grep: no hits) and the cited range is unrelated code. It named
`ResumeEntry` and `ResumeEntry.callsite`; the only `ResumeEntry` in the tree is
`BackendResumeEntry` in src/ir_interp/, unrelated.

Its proposed fix -- `ResumeEntry.callsite -> Vec<CallSiteId>`, or a pre-folded
any-callsite-requires-carrier bit -- DOES NOT APPLY. Because callsite is part of
position identity, folding callsites together would merge positions that must
stay distinct. The correct shape is one `ResumePayload` position per
(entry, callsite) pair, matching what `call_return_flow` already mints.

The `merge_callsite_activation` sibling is still at semantic.rs:186 and still
fixed, so the "same disease family" framing stands.

## Checks

- `required_resume_transport_positions` emits one position per delivering
  callsite, so its output set equals the set `call_return_flow` produces for the
  same executable.
- A regression on the if/else repro asserts a `ContinuationEntry` seam fact
  exists for BOTH branch callsites, not one.
- A deliberately-asymmetric case (branches whose calls have different return
  transport shapes joining one entry) proves the two positions get independently
  solved layouts.
- Full lib + matrix green.
title: required_resume_transport_positions drops all but one callsite when several deliver into one resume entry
